description: Cross-language SIMULATION-OUTPUT DERIVATION conformance (streaming-output-sinks RFC §7-§9, §16.12). The derivation turns (.esm document + flat state element names + caller-named observed subset) into the dimension-labeled, CF-annotated output plan a Zarr writer is handed. It exists in Julia (`pkg/EarthSciAST.jl/src/data_output.jl`) and Rust (`pkg/earthsci-ast-rs/src/data_output.rs`) and had NO cross-language gate at all until this corpus: EarthSciIO's `conformance/write_spec.json` is an ALREADY-DERIVED schema, so the write corpus starts downstream of derivation and drives the three writers from a hand-authored shape. A derivation corpus's OUTPUT type is that write corpus's INPUT type, so the two chain end to end: .esm -> [derivation, here] -> OutputSchema -> [writers, EarthSciIO] -> Zarr store.

scope_excluded.python: no derivation counterpart exists; EarthSciIO's Python track is a WRITER, which consumes an already-derived schema

inputs.document: the .esm fixture, parsed as-is (no build, no solve)
inputs.slot_names: the flat state element names in flat order — element i of the list is flat index i. This is the runner's `state_variable_names`, following the column-major `name[i,j,...]` cell-key scheme (RFC §7), which is byte-identical across bindings.
inputs.observed: the caller-named observed/derived fields to write alongside the state (RFC decision 8). A declared `observed` variable that has a slot but is NOT named here is dropped from the plan.

contract.flat_indices: 0-BASED flat-state indices in ROW-MAJOR (C-order) cell order within `shape` — the layout a Zarr writer consumes, with the column-major->row-major transposition already applied. Julia's `VarGridding` stores 1-based indices in enumeration order plus a `cart` map; `row_major_flat_indices` converts, so both bindings compare on one representation.
contract.var_dims: the ON-DISK dimension list: the record axis FIRST, then the variable's spatial axes. A scalar's dims are therefore exactly [time_dim].
contract.grid_order: first-seen spatial-dim-signature order; the signature is the SORTED SET of a variable's dim names, so axis order does not fragment a grid and every scalar (empty signature) lands in ONE shared 0-D grid.
contract.var_order: sorted by base name within a grid (the derivation sorts groups by base name so a derived schema is reproducible).

cases.notes: The case that exposed the divergence: four scalars, ONE grid, every variable's dims exactly [time]. The observed `flux` has a slot AND is requested, so it is written.
Same document and same flat state, but the caller names no observed field, so `Box.flux` is DROPPED (RFC decision 8: output is the state plus a caller-named subset, not every observed).

Two variables on one 3x2 [lon, lat] grid. Cell keys are listed in the column-major order a build emits them (dim 0 fastest); the golden's row-major `flat_indices` are the transposition. Both axes carry `coordinates` entries, so both CF dimension coordinates are planned.

Scalar AND gridded in one document over two spatial signatures => exactly THREE grids. With a synthetic singleton axis per scalar it would be five, which is what makes this the fixture a shape-signature grouping bug shows up in. The record axis is `t`, so a binding that assumes the name `time` fails here.
